# Abstract

This gazetteer compiles WGS84 coordinates, active occupational spans and benchmark population series for 588 catalogued habitation settlements and residential complexes (1.936 benchmark observations, averaging 3,29 per site) across Arizona Hydrological Unit 15 from 9500BC to 1600AD [@kelly2025; @bird2022p3k14c]. The inventory spans major Salt-Gila Hohokam canal centres (S-Kiukchu'k, Pueblo Grande, Sivan Vah'ki, Los Muertos, Cashion Ruin, Escalante, Grand Canal), Mogollon and San Pedro-Tucson settlements (Los Morteros-Point of Pines, Grasshopper Pueblo, Babocomari Village, 3-Up, Apache Creek Pueblo, Bailey Ruin), Hopi, Zuni and Sinagua pueblos (Orayvi, Hawikku, Homol'ovi, Halona:wa, Awatovi, Chaves Pass, Mats'a:kya, Wupatki), Lower Colorado and Lower Gila centres (Fitzmaurice Ruin, Gatlin Site, Palo Verde Ruin, Van Liere Ruin, Gillespie Dam, Needles (Mohave)) and early desert sites (Tule Springs, Los Morteros, Tinajas Altas, Santa Cruz Bend, Tumamoc Hill) [@haury1976hohokam; @fish2007hohokam; @reid1999grasshopper; @adams2002homolovi]. Source-ledger reconciliation accounts for 588 included settlements and 736 excluded records (731 duplicate-alias consolidations and 5 unquantified cave exclusions) across all 1.324 evaluated candidates with zero unaccounted entries.

# Background

Nucleated settlements across HU 15 reflect desert hydraulic engineering, alluvial flood-recession farming and defensive plateau aggregation. In the Phoenix Basin, S-Kiukchu'k (3,2k at 1000AD) anchored Pioneer through Sedentary canal irrigation before Classic Period platform-mound centres expanded at Pueblo Grande (3,1k in 1300AD), Sivan Vah'ki (2,6k in 1300AD) and Los Muertos (1,4k in 1350AD) [@haury1976hohokam; @fish2007hohokam].

Across the Tucson Basin, San Pedro Valley and Mogollon Rim, early agricultural camps (Los Morteros, Santa Cruz Bend, Tumamoc Hill) preceded large aggregated villages including Los Morteros-Point of Pines (1,35k in 1200AD), Grasshopper Pueblo (1,1k in 1300AD), 3-Up (1,06k), Apache Creek Pueblo (1,06k) and Babocomari Village (1,06k) [@hill2004southwest; @reid1999grasshopper]. On the Little Colorado Plateau, Pueblo III-IV coalescence sustained Wupatki (1,06k), Chaves Pass (1,15k in 1375AD), Homol'ovi (1,45k in 1400AD), Orayvi (2,1k in 1600AD), Hawikku (1,65k in 1500AD), Halona:wa (1,25k in 1540AD), Awatovi (1,2k in 1540AD) and Mats'a:kya (1,15k in 1540AD) [@adams2002homolovi; @smith1966hawikuh].

# Methodology

## Gazetteer Compilation and Ledger Screening

Each candidate site was checked against CENTAUR gazetteer criteria requiring documented WGS84 coordinates, dated architectural or radiocarbon horizons and quantified residential population series [@bird2022p3k14c; @kelly2025]. Early quantified loci such as Tule Springs (9500BC to 6000BC, 30 peak), Tinajas Altas (1000BC to 1100AD, 35 peak) and Cibola Spring (1250AD to 1325AD, 240 peak) enter the 588-site inventory, whereas 731 matching-name duplicate twins located within 2 km of canonical centroids and 5 unquantified non-habitation cave records remain excluded in the archival source ledger [@smith1966hawikuh]. All benchmark years follow GMT+0.

## Room-Count and Compound Demography

Puebloan and Mogollon site figures derive from excavated and surface-mapped room counts adjusted by contemporaneous occupation ratios, roof-area coefficients and tree-ring construction phases [@reid1999grasshopper; @adams2002homolovi; @robinson2021dendro]. Hohokam estimates integrate mapped courtyard-group and compound areas with regional canal-command population models [@haury1976hohokam; @hill2004southwest; @fish2007hohokam].

# Testing and Validation

Ledger reconciliation records exact agreement across 588 included settlements and 736 excluded records (731 duplicate-alias consolidations and 5 unquantified cave exclusions), totalling 1.324 evaluated candidates (Table \ref{tab:coverage-sett-arizona}) with zero unaccounted entries. Sub-regional counts cluster heavily on the Little Colorado Plateau (316 sites, 53,7%, 1.058 observations) and the Salt-Verde-Middle Gila Core (191 sites, 32,5%, 626 observations), followed by the Santa Cruz-San Pedro-Cochise Highlands (60 sites, 10,2%, 194 observations) and the Lower Colorado corridor (21 sites, 3,6%, 58 observations). Chronological cross-checks capture the Hohokam-to-Pueblo IV demographic shift: S-Kiukchu'k (3,2k in 1000AD) declines ahead of Classic maxima at Pueblo Grande (3,1k) and Sivan Vah'ki (2,6k) in 1300AD, after which Salt-Gila centres contract sharply while Hopi and Zuni towns (Orayvi, Hawikku, Homol'ovi, Halona:wa, Awatovi) sustain large populations through 1400AD to 1600AD [@hill2004southwest; @adams2002homolovi; @robinson2021dendro].

```{r tab-coverage, results='asis'}
reg_list <- mod_json$regions
s_reg <- vapply(sett_json, function (e) as.character(e$region_id), character(1))
s_obs <- vapply(sett_json, function (e) length(e$population), integer(1))
s_pk <- vapply(sett_json, function (e) max(unlist(e$population)), numeric(1))
s_nm <- vapply(sett_json, function (e) as.character(e$name), character(1))
cov_rows <- lapply(names(reg_list), function (rk) {
  idx <- which(s_reg == rk)
  best <- idx[which.max(s_pk[idx])]
  data.frame(
    Subregion = gsub("/", " and ", gsub(" & ", " and ", sub("^\\d+\\.\\s*", "", reg_list[[rk]]$name))),
    Sites = viscount_fmt_number(length(idx), 0L),
    Share = paste0(viscount_fmt_number(100 * length(idx) / length(sett_json), 1L), "%"),
    Obs = viscount_fmt_number(sum(s_obs[idx]), 0L),
    TopSite = paste0(s_nm[best], " (", viscount_fmt_pop(s_pk[best]), ")"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
df_cov <- do.call(rbind, cov_rows)
rownames(df_cov) <- NULL
viscount_table(
  df_cov,
  "Sub-regional distribution of the 588 catalogued settlements and benchmark observations across Arizona HU 15.",
  c("Sub-Region", "Sites", "Share", "Obs.", "Leading Site (Peak)"),
  list(label = "tab:coverage-sett-arizona", font_size = "scriptsize")
)
```

# Results

## Leading Settlement Gazetteer

Table \ref{tab:gazetteer-arizona} reports the Top 45 settlements ranked by peak population descending out of the 588 catalogued settlements in HU 15, and Figure \ref{fig:settlements-arizona} displays the 588-site rank-size curve and the leading fifteen centres led by S-Kiukchu'k (3,2k), Pueblo Grande (3,1k), Sivan Vah'ki (2,6k) and Orayvi (2,1k), followed by the 112-site modal architectural tier at 1,06k.

```{r tab-gazetteer, results='asis'}
fmt_cell_pop <- function (p) {
  if (is.null(p) || is.na(p)) return("-")
  viscount_fmt_pop(p)
}
fmt_yr_era <- function (y) {
  if (y < 0L) paste0(abs(y), "BC") else paste0(y, "AD")
}
pk_vec <- vapply(sett_json, function (e) max(unlist(e$population)), numeric(1))
nm_vec <- vapply(sett_json, function (e) as.character(e$name), character(1))
ord_idx <- order(-pk_vec, nm_vec)
top_setts <- sett_json[ord_idx[seq_len(min(45L, length(ord_idx)))]]
rows <- lapply(top_setts, function (e) {
  yrs <- sort(as.integer(names(e$population)))
  pk <- max(unlist(e$population))
  span_str <- if (min(yrs) == max(yrs)) fmt_yr_era(min(yrs)) else paste0(fmt_yr_era(min(yrs)), "-", fmt_yr_era(max(yrs)))
  coord_str <- paste0(viscount_fmt_number(e$coords[[1]], 2L), ", ", viscount_fmt_number(e$coords[[2]], 2L))
  data.frame(
    Settlement = e$name,
    State = e$country,
    Coords = coord_str,
    Span = span_str,
    Peak = viscount_fmt_pop(pk),
    Y800 = fmt_cell_pop(e$population[["800"]]),
    Y1100 = fmt_cell_pop(e$population[["1100"]]),
    Y1300 = fmt_cell_pop(e$population[["1300"]]),
    Y1500 = fmt_cell_pop(e$population[["1500"]]),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
df_gaz <- do.call(rbind, rows)
rownames(df_gaz) <- NULL
viscount_table(
  df_gaz,
  "Top 45 Hohokam, Mogollon, Puebloan and Yuman settlements in Arizona HU 15 ranked by peak population.",
  c("Settlement", "State", "Coords (Lat, Lon)", "Span", "Peak", "800AD", "1100AD", "1300AD", "1500AD"),
  list(label = "tab:gazetteer-arizona", font_size = "scriptsize")
)
```

```{r fig-settlements, results='asis'}
viscount_figure(
  "figures/fig4_arizona_settlements.png",
  "Rank-size distribution and leading fifteen centres across the 588 catalogued settlements in Arizona HU 15.",
  "fig:settlements-arizona"
)
```

## Source Ledger Audit

Table \ref{tab:ledger-arizona} lists the first 30 of 731 consolidated duplicate-alias candidate records (alongside 5 unquantified cave exclusions for 736 total exclusions) accounting together with the 588 included settlements for all 1.324 evaluated entries in the Arizona HU 15 source ledger.

```{r tab-ledger, results='asis'}
exc_cands <- Filter(function (cnd) identical(cnd$reason, "duplicate_alias"), ledger_json$candidates)
if (length(exc_cands) > 30L) exc_cands <- exc_cands[seq_len(30L)]
l_rows <- lapply(exc_cands, function (cnd) {
  data.frame(
    Candidate = cnd$name,
    State = cnd$country,
    Status = cnd$status,
    Reason = gsub("_", " ", cnd$reason),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
df_led <- do.call(rbind, l_rows)
rownames(df_led) <- NULL
viscount_table(
  df_led,
  "Representative consolidated duplicate-alias candidate records (first 30 of 731) from the 1.324 evaluated entries in Arizona HU 15.",
  c("Candidate", "Jurisdiction", "Status", "Ledger Classification"),
  list(label = "tab:ledger-arizona", font_size = "scriptsize")
)
```

# Limitations

Three limitations apply to HU 15 site records. First, large Phoenix Basin centres such as Pueblo Grande and Sivan Vah'ki sit beneath modern urban or protected monumental zones, restricting excavation of outer pithouse residential rings [@fish2007hohokam]. Second, 112 Southwest Social Networks sites share a standardised 1.060-inhabitant regional tier cap rather than site-specific excavated floor estimates, producing a horizontal shelf in the upper rank-size curve (Figure \ref{fig:settlements-arizona}). Third, dispersed Yuman floodplain settlements along the lower Colorado River near Needles and Fort Yuma shifted channels frequently after seasonal floods, leaving diffuse archaeological footprints.
